summary: The checker report is clean (D-0 to D-12 ok), and all three faults from last round are fixed. The mercenary read is now "Has a price.", the protection noun is now "safety", the ladder line no longer starts a sentence with {scale}, and the summon-busy lines no longer assume a post. Reading the slots turns up three new faults. Debrief lines that put the approach verb straight after "by", "to", "took" or "refused" read wrongly for ask and pay. The first word line gives "a family" for a family tie. The loyal read says "odd approaches", but the GDD says "any approach".

faults.fault: Slot reading, debrief: {approach} is filled with the approach verb (ask, pay, help, pressure). turned-how gives "Sunita Ferrer turned by ask. Cost: $0." and "said yes to pay." refused gives "refused ask" and "turned down pay." not-yet gives "took ask but wants more." These are wrong for ask and pay (and "turned by help" is odd), so any contact turned or refused that way reads badly.
faults.fix: Put the approach in a form that works for every verb, e.g. "{who} turned. Approach: {approach}. Cost: {price}.", "{who} said no to the {approach} approach." or "{who} answered {approach}". Apply the same to refused and not-yet.

faults.fault: Slot reading, debrief word: "Word of {fact} went from {who} to {to}, a {tie}." puts a tie kind after "a". It reads for workmate, regular or rival, but for family it gives "...to Dimitra Marchetti, a family." That is wrong for every word passed along a family tie.
faults.fix: Use the tie as a modifier, as the second line does: "...to {to}, along a {tie} tie." or "...to {to} ({tie} tie)."

faults.fault: Temperament fit, reads: the loyal read "Reports odd approaches." says a Loyal person reports only unusual approaches. The Temperament Spec says a Loyal person under a Menace campaign "Reports any approach", so the Scout's read misleads the player about the risk.
faults.fix: Reword to match the rule, e.g. "Reports any approach." or "Any approach goes in the report."
